subject: tech
title: Patterns and Loops
about: A pattern repeats, and a loop tells a computer to do the same steps again instead of writing them over and over (K2-AP-03). The cards find what comes next, count how many times a part repeats, and spot loops in real life, like brushing every tooth and the days of the week. Read it together and say each pattern out loud; hearing the rhythm is half the fun.
tip: Clap a pattern like clap, clap, stomp, and ask him to say the repeating part before he joins in.

cards.q: Doing the same steps again and again has a name. What is it called?
cards.note: Loop is the word for repeating steps. Brushing each tooth and a clock going round are loops too.

cards.sayQ: A pattern: red, blue, red, blue, red. What comes next?
cards.note: The pattern is red, blue, over and over. After red comes blue.

cards.sayQ: A pattern: star, moon, star, moon, star, moon. What comes next?
cards.note: Star, moon, star, moon. The pattern starts again with a star.

cards.sayQ: A pattern: apple, apple, banana, apple, apple, banana, apple, apple. What comes next?
cards.note: The repeating part is apple, apple, banana. Two apples are done, so a banana is next.

cards.sayQ: A pattern: red, blue, star, red, blue, star, red. What comes next?
cards.note: Three things repeat: red, blue, star. After red comes blue.

cards.q: Clap, clap, stomp. Clap, clap, stomp. Clap, clap... What comes next?
cards.note: Clap, clap, stomp is the part that repeats. Say it with your body!

cards.sayQ: A pattern: dog, cat, dog, cat, dog, cat. Which part repeats?
cards.note: Find the smallest piece that comes back again and again. Here it is dog, cat.

cards.q: 🔴 🔵 🔴 🔵 🔴 🔵 How many times does red, blue repeat?
cards.sayQ: A pattern: red, blue, red, blue, red, blue. How many times does red, blue repeat?
cards.note: Red, blue is one time. Count the pairs: one, two, three.

cards.q: Which is the short way to say clap, clap, clap, clap, clap?
cards.note: A loop says the step once and how many times. Clap 5 times, done!

cards.q: You want a robot to hop 3 times. Which is the short way to tell it?
cards.note: A loop is shorter to say and shorter to write. That is why programs use them.

cards.q: A robot is told: jump 4 times. How many jumps does it do?
cards.note: The loop runs the step jump four times, then stops.

cards.q: You brush each tooth the same way, tooth after tooth. What is that like?
cards.note: Brush, move over, brush, move over: the same steps again and again is a loop.

cards.q: The clock hand goes all the way round. What does it do next?
cards.note: Round and round, then again. The clock is a loop that never ends.

cards.q: The days of the week go round and round. What day comes after Sunday?
cards.note: After the last day, the week starts again. The days of the week are a loop.
A pattern has a part that repeats. Red, blue, red, blue repeats red, blue.

cards.sayQ: A pattern: soccer ball, basketball, soccer ball, basketball. What are the next two?
cards.note: Keep the same order: soccer ball first, then basketball.

cards.q: A loop says: stir 10 times. When does the stirring stop?
cards.note: A loop runs its steps the number of times you say, then stops.
